title.narrative: BiH Second Health Sectors Programmatic Development Policy Loan

description.narrative: This program document proposes a Second Health Sectors Development Policy Loan (DPL) operation totaling US75 million dollars equivalent for Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH), which forms an integral part of broader World Bank assistance to the health sectors in BiH. Criteria for selecting policy areas and pillars reflect the authorities demand and the World Bank's value-added and comparative advantage in the health sector. Extensive collaboration with the authorities on these reforms has occurred since 2019. The objective of this proposed operation, the second and last in a programmatic series, is to improve the financial sustainability of the healthcare sectors and the quality of care in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH) and Republika Srpska (RS). This DPL complements the ongoing Health Systems Improvement Project (P171150) and benefits from the complementary technical assistance (TA) provided by the World Bank and other development partners to support the overall strengthening of the health sectors. This holistic approach by the World Bank is further complemented by the EU4Health program 2021-2027, signed with the BiH authorities in July 2024. The first DPL in the programmatic series was approved by the Board of Executive Directors in March 2023.
To improve the financial sustainability of the health care sectors and the quality of care.

title.narrative: 8. In FBiH, increase in the ratio of processed applications for environmental permits compared to those received in a given year (% of total)

comment.narrative: Target achieved in 2022 (76%) and 2023 (78%). Ministry of environment is processing data for 2024, preliminary findings on track, will be available towards end 2025 target.

title.narrative: 6. In RS, the proportion of primary health centers that report implementation of the electronic referral over the past year (% of total)

comment.narrative: Target achieved. All primary health centers are integreted in IZIS and use electronic referral.

title.narrative: 5. In RS, cumulative number of girls that received HPV vaccination between 11 and 14 years of age

comment.narrative: Target achieved, per available data received from RS MOF. HPV vaccination received 2895 kids out of which 2061 girls age 11 to 14.

title.narrative: 7. Compliance with FBiH legislation on tobacco - on an ordinal scale from 0 to 10 control

comment.narrative: As planned, the implementation of the bylaws (Regulation on the conditions for special smoking areas in terms of exceptions to the smoking ''Official Gazette of the Federation of BiH'', No. 41/24, and Regulation on the form and content of signs prohibiting the sale and prohibition of smoking to minors ''Official Gazette of the Federation of BiH'', No. 41/24) for restricting smoking in closed and public places started in May 2025, and fines for violations began being enforced in June 2025. Overall, we have observed sufficient compliance with the legislation, as confirmed by media reports. However, a formal evaluation will be provided by the end of 2025.
